q: The charge of an object is $+3.2 \cdot 10^{-19}\,\text{C}$. How many electrons is the object missing?
a: Charge is made of elementary charges, so $n = Q : e = 3.2 \cdot 10^{-19}\,\text{C} : 1.602 \cdot 10^{-19}\,\text{C} \approx 2$. The object is missing two electrons, and that is why it is positive.

q: Both charges of two point charges are doubled, and at the same time the distance between them is doubled. How does the force between them change?
a: The force does not change. The product of the charges becomes four times as large, and the denominator $r^2$ of Coulomb's law also becomes four times as large, so they cancel: $\tfrac{2 \cdot 2}{2^2} = 1$.
